criteria.accept_quiet_window: Keep the probe exactly as the worker left it: 5s per-delivery mail deadline, 8 phases, 30+ `canlc run` sender invocations. Document that live runs require a quiet machine (1-minute load under roughly 35-40), serialize the F01 rerun alone, and accept that the probe fails under parallel-worker load. No rework, no re-verification loop.
criteria.patient_timeouts: Raise the probe's per-delivery mail timeout toward the baseline's 30s phase budget while keeping every verdict identical (still real staged deliveries through the real Can sender, still judged on mailbox content). Run one fresh live verification of the retimed probe, then keep the standard gates. Costs one worker rework loop; the retired .py files stay retired.

a02_durability.instructions: How should the migration dispose the load-sensitive A02 signup probe so its verdicts stay durable without misrepresenting production timing?

state.durability_stakes: The checklist's F01 step needs runnable reruns of every retired port, and the goal counts a record only when its baseline obligation is actually fulfilled. A probe that passes solely in rare quiet windows is a fragile obligation: future reruns fail unless the whole machine idles. The 256 GB MacBook normally carries 3 parallel workers at 40-60+ load; quiet windows occur only when at most one light task runs.
state.load_evidence: The worker's green run (rc=0, 27 checks) took 38 minutes in a quiet window and it reports each delivery needs about 7.6 CPU-s inside the fixed 5s mail deadline, requiring 1-minute load under roughly 35-40. The coordinator's three reruns under load 60+ failed: twice code 10 (stage) and once code 20 (spawn) after 43m34s. Build holds at 124/124 regardless of load.
state.mandate: Can is an AI-agent-authored language with no backwards-compatibility obligations; the standing rule prefers reaching the migration goal over scaffolding and nested proof layers. tests/auth_signup/probe.py and tests/auth_signup/fake_mail.py are already retired (5ec1cdb) for tests/auth_signup/probe/; the decision is whether to rework the living probe or accept its operating envelope.
state.production_timing: The sender under test delivers in fractions of a second (the Python baseline's 30s budget per phase group never binds). The 7.6 CPU-s per delivery is Can toolchain boot inside each `canlc run` sender invocation, not production mail latency. The probe's 5s mail deadline therefore times toolchain startup, not the behavior under test; the production property (a real delivery lands in the mailbox) is timing-agnostic.
state.worker_record: The A02 worker iterated honestly against real behavior (empty-grandchild environment discovery, expire tolerance, P1 split into one-delivery driver runs) across 10 commits and documented the load constraint itself. Its tamper and bad-canlc controls bite. The open question is durability of the accepted artifact, not the good faith of the port.
